aAbout: Flightradar24 shows real-time aircraft positions built from ADS-B, MLAT, radar and FAA data fed by roughly 45,000 volunteer receivers, with airport departure and arrival boards, aircraft photos and deep flight history. Its consumer plans layer on features — up to 365 days of history, full aircraft details (age, serial, squawk, vertical speed), 15+ weather layers, aeronautical charts and oceanic tracks — and its iOS/Android apps, including 3D and cockpit views, are widely considered the best in flight tracking.
aStrengths: Flightradar24 is the deeper tool for watching the sky itself: a receiver network of roughly 45,000 feeders, up to 365 days of flight history, full aircraft details, 15+ live weather layers, ATC boundaries, aeronautical charts, oceanic tracks, CSV export and airport boards with live ETAs. Its apps are best-in-class for planespotting, and it reports more than 1,000,000 subscribers across its plans.
bAbout: ADS-B Exchange is a global platform that aggregates and displays real-time aircraft movements via a collaborative network of contributors, offering, in its own words, a transparent view of the skies without censorship or filtering. Individuals and organisations host ADS-B receivers that capture broadcast data directly from aircraft, including military, commercial and private traffic. ADS-B Exchange claims over 25,000 active receivers and positions updated every 500 milliseconds, offers a history function on the map back to March 2020, and sells enterprise live and daily data products alongside the public map — with no public pricing for those enterprise products.
bStrengths: ADS-B Exchange is the honesty champion of flight data: it never filters or obfuscates, so military, government and blocked aircraft appear when commercial sites hide them. It claims positions updated every 500 milliseconds, a map history back to March 2020, and high-fidelity archives, on a network it claims is the world's largest independent ADS-B receiver network at over 25,000 receivers. For researchers, journalists and enthusiasts investigating traffic other trackers suppress, that raw, unfiltered view is the point.
betterAnswer: They solve different problems. Flightradar24 is the better everyday tracker: richer aircraft detail, up to 365 days of history, airport boards and the best apps — filtered, and with the depth behind subscriptions. ADS-B Exchange is the better open record: a community-fed map that shows every broadcast as received, including military and private traffic, with history back to March 2020 and a cheap personal ad-free tier. If you want a tracker, open Flightradar24; if you want the unfiltered sky, open ADS-B Exchange.

intro: Flightradar24 and ADS-B Exchange track the same sky with opposite philosophies. Flightradar24 (Sweden, founded 2006) is the polished mainstream tracker: real-time positions from a vast volunteer receiver network, rich aircraft detail, airport boards and best-in-class apps, with some traffic filtered and the depth sold by subscription. ADS-B Exchange, founded in 2016 by an aviation enthusiast, is a community-fed network built on the opposite promise — a transparent view of the skies without censorship or filtering, displaying all aircraft broadcasts as received, including military and private aircraft other trackers hide.
pricingA: Free Basic tier with limited features. pricingB: The live map is free with ads. Enterprise data products (live positions, live operations, daily positions and daily operations) have no public pricing — commercial use is by contact and subscription sale only.

verdictA: Choose Flightradar24 if you track for the love of it or for travel — planespotting, following aircraft globally, digging into history and aircraft detail, checking airport boards, or wanting the best mobile apps and 3D views.
verdictB: Choose ADS-B Exchange if seeing everything matters more than polish — military and private traffic shown as received, a long map history, and a researcher-oriented, community-fed map, even if that means ads on the free tier and a more technical interface.
verdictLine: Flightradar24 is the polished product — filtered, app-first and subscription-deep. ADS-B Exchange is the open record — unfiltered, community-fed and built for people who want the broadcasts as received. Casual users will be happier in Flightradar24; enthusiasts and researchers who resent filtering will choose ADS-B Exchange.
worldEye: If you mainly want to glance at the sky rather than study it, WorldEye shows live flights free on a 3D globe — no signup — alongside live ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes, wildfires and 74,229 public cameras across 109 countries in the same view. WorldEye does not claim unfiltered military data like ADS-B Exchange or Flightradar24-grade flight history; it is the free, everything-at-once picture. An optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds the OSINT toolkit and intel feeds.
